translationRepairs: Dong Zhuo's forced removal of the court unleashed chaos: depositories from the Academy to the Hongdu archive were looted wholesale; bolts of silk that had carried the classics were torn up for tent hangings or cut into money purses.

When Dong Zhuo shifted the capital, officials and commoners were thrown into turmoil; from the Circular Moat, Eastern Pavilion, Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Xuanming, and Hongdu repositories the stored ordinances and writings were plundered and scattered together; as for the silken books, large pieces were joined into curtains and canopies, and small ones were cut into pouches.
Idiomatic omits named repositories present in the Chinese (Stone Chamber, Xuanming, etc.) and invents 'money purses' for □囊.
